steps.label: Definition
lines: Formal charge: the charge assigned to an
atom in a Lewis structure, calculated by
taking the difference between the valence
electrons of the free atom and the
electrons assigned to that atom in the
steps.why: The definition is a counting rule, not a real charge: it assumes every shared pair is split equally between the two bonded atoms.
common_mistakes: Calling formal charge the real charge on the atom. It is a counting device for comparing Lewis structures.
Leaving out in a Lewis structure — formal charge has no meaning outside one.
steps.memory_tip: What the free atom had, minus what the structure gives it.
steps.margin_note: The phrase in a Lewis structure anchors the definition.

lines: V = valence electrons of the free atom,
Ex: central O of ozone: 6 − 2 − ½(6) = +1.
steps.why: The three symbols split the atom's electrons into kept and shared; halving B is the equal-sharing assumption from the definition.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the half on B. Only half of each shared pair is assigned to the atom.
Swapping N and B when reading a structure quickly.
steps.memory_tip: Keep all lone electrons, keep half the shared ones, subtract both from V.
